newsitem.title: HONG KONG: U.S. expects China to keep promises to HK - envoy.
newsitem.headline: U.S. expects China to keep promises to HK - envoy.

text.p: The United States expects Beijing to abide by its promise to accord Hong Kong a high degree of self-rule after the territory reverts to China this year, a U.S. envoy said on Friday.

Stuart Eizenstat, under-secretary of commerce for international trade, also said the Hong Kong issue will figure prominently in the agenda of the United States in its pursuit of a "sustained and productive dialogue with China".
"The United States takes a strong interest in Hong Kong's future and expects China to adhere to the 1984 Sino-British Joint Declaration," Eizenstat said in a speech to business leaders in Hong Kong.

The Joint Declaration committed Britain to relinquishing sovereignty of its last Asian colony, and requires China to accord the territory of just six million people considerable autonomy in running their affairs and leaving them free to maintain their capitalist way of life.

"Over the next few months, the American public, Congress and media will be keenly focussed on a few key issues in the relationship including market opening, non-proliferation, human rights, the trade deficit, and the reversion of Hong Kong," he said.
Hong Kong, a British colony for more than 150 years, reverts to China at midnight June 30.
Many people in the wealthy colony are dismayed by China's plans to dismantle its elected legislature and amend some of its laws protecting rights and civil liberties.
Eizenstat said the United States had seen mixed signals from Beijing and would be watching developments in Hong Kong.

He said Washington was pleased that Beijing had permitted principal government officials to remain in their posts but was concerned about China's plan to replace Hong Kong's elected chamber with one carefully crafted by Beijing.
"The United States remains concerned about the decision to replace the elected Legislative Council with a provisional legislature appointed by Beijing," Eizenstat said.
